title: an external project's new branch uses the captain-confirmed branch_prefix so the repository CI runs on it, a round refuses a new branch that no recorded CI trigger pattern matches, the task grammar reads a task id after one leading path segment everywhere, and onboarding proposes the prefix and CI patterns from the CI files and recent branches
acceptance: Why. The captain (2026-10-07) saw that firstmate opened an external pull request from a branch named `t-001-work`, which the repository CI never runs on, and said verbatim: "t-001-work 你開的feature branch naming沒有遵照公司repo規定, 不會觸發CI, 你提PR之前應該要先調查好會執行CI的branch name prefix", then "從根本修". Today bin/fm-worker.sh:417-461 names a new external branch `$slug-work` (:458) with no knowledge of the CI trigger rules. One managed repository's CI pipeline runs only on pushes to refs/heads/{develop,master,hotfix/*,feature/*,support/*,release/*,security/*,preview/pr-*,deployer/*}; another's pipeline trigger lives in an imported local jsonnet file (`trigger: utils.default_trigger`) and also lists feature/*; most merged pull requests in every managed repository use a `feature/` head branch. The branch-to-task grammar (bin/fm-emit.sh:41-47 `fm_task_of_branch`, the TypeScript twin at board/server.ts:638-641) only reads a task id at the start of the branch name, so a prefixed branch names no task.

Change 1, fields (bin/lib/fm_conventions.py). Three optional data-only CONVENTIONS front-matter fields, captain-confirmed like the pr_* fields: `branch_prefix` (a string matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,30}/$, one path segment ending in a slash, e.g. "feature/"), `ci_branch_patterns` (a JSON list of 1-30 non-empty strings, each a branch glob such as "feature/*" or a ref glob such as "refs/heads/feature/*"), and `ci_pull_request` (bool: the CI also runs on pull_request events). `validate` refuses any other shape with a message naming the field. The private owner default file (FM_HOME/owners/<owner>.yaml, read by `pr_format` at :51-79) may also carry `branch_prefix` (only that one of the three; `ci_branch_patterns`/`ci_pull_request` there are refused as an unknown owner field, because CI rules belong to one repository). Precedence for branch_prefix: CONVENTIONS > owner default > none. `pr_format` accepts an owner file that also holds `branch_prefix` and still returns only the three pr_* keys (tests/lib/external_pr_format.py:139-146 compares that exact dict). A string value is JSON-quoted in both files ("feature/"), as parse_fields (:42-46) requires. A new CLI field `--field branch_format` prints JSON `{"prefix": <string or "">, "patterns": <list or null>, "pull_request": <bool>}`; patterns is null when CONVENTIONS has no `ci_branch_patterns`. The worker reads it through the existing `fm_conventions` wrapper (bin/fm-config.sh:1140-1146), unchanged.

Change 2, the worker branch (bin/fm-worker.sh). For an external project only (FM_EXTERNAL=1), before the branch guess at :417, read `fm_conventions branch_format`; when that call fails (for example a malformed owner file), the worker prints `fm-worker: cannot read branch format: <stderr>`, emits worker_crashed with that text as --en and `fm-worker：無法讀取 branch 格式：<stderr>` as --tw and exits 65 before any worktree, push or pull request (the same refusal shape as adopt_refuse), because a guessed prefix could publish a branch CI never runs. Every new call in the slice that tests/external-execution.test.sh:262-272 lifts (from `if [ -n "$branch_guess" ]; then` to `case "$branch" in main|master`) is guarded by an empty-prefix default so that harness, which defines no fm_conventions, still yields `t-051-work`; the Change 3 check sits after that `case`. The guess at :418-427 (local refs, then origin heads) matches `^<escaped prefix>?<slug>-` case-insensitively, so it still finds an existing unprefixed `t-NNN-work` branch and also a prefixed `<prefix>t-NNN-…` one. When no branch is found and the task adopts no PR, the new branch is `<prefix><slug>-<short>` when a prefix is set, where <short> is built from the spec's `public_title` only when `fm_public_text.validate(public_title, public_summary, style='plain', changes=public_changes)` (bin/lib/fm_public_text.py, the same check the pull request text uses later at :2161-2174) returns no problem: the title lowercased, every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] turned into one hyphen, cut to 40 characters and stripped of edge hyphens; in every other case (public_title null, empty, or failing that check, or the slug empty) <short> is `work`, so unchecked text never reaches a public branch name; with no prefix the branch stays `$slug-work` exactly as today. An adopted PR (T-237 `adopt`) keeps its own branch and skips Change 3. The self project (FM_EXTERNAL=0) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Change 3, the CI trigger check (bin/fm-worker.sh). Right after a new external branch name is chosen (only when the branch did not exist; never for an existing branch or an adopted PR) and before any commit, push or pull request: if branch_format.patterns is null, print one line `fm-worker: no CI branch patterns recorded for this project; cannot prove CI runs on <branch>` and continue (migration). Else, if branch_format.pull_request is true, continue. Else match the branch against every pattern after stripping a leading `refs/heads/` from the pattern, with Python fnmatch.fnmatchcase semantics; if none matches, refuse: print `fm-worker: branch <branch> matches no CI trigger pattern (<patterns joined by comma>); set branch_prefix in the project conventions`, emit the existing `worker_crashed` event type with that text as --en and `fm-worker：branch <branch> 不符合任何 CI 觸發規則（<patterns>）；請在專案 conventions 設定 branch_prefix` as --tw (as `adopt_refuse` at :432-436 passes both; every variable in the --tw text is braced, because bash 3.2 reads a CJK character after `$name` as part of the name), exit 65, and make no worktree commit, no push and no pull request.

Change 4, one task grammar with an optional prefix, in a new pure library (bin/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh; board/server.ts :638-641 between the task grammar markers). The shell grammar block moves out of bin/fm-emit.sh into bin/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh, a sourced library that only defines and runs nothing, with the `# fm:sourced` and `# shellcheck shell=bash` header lines that bin/lib/fm-stack.sh:1-2 uses. Exactly these definitions move: FM_TASK_DIG, FM_TASK_UP, FM_TASK_LOW, FM_TASK_ID, fm_task_is, fm_task_of_branch, fm_task_of_title and fm_task_of_pr. FM_TASK_KEY, fm_task_key, fm_task_of_key, FM_OWNED_ID and fm_decision_id stay in fm-emit.sh. fm-emit.sh sources the library relative to its own path, `. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh"`, before those remaining definitions, so fm-decide.sh, fm-merge.sh, fm-diagram.sh and the autopilot, which source fm-emit.sh, keep every name they read today. The three comments that name fm-emit.sh as the one home of the shell grammar (bin/fm-emit.sh:25-29, board/server.ts:617-620 and design/design.md §5.2 :320-325) name the library instead. Fixtures that copy fm-emit.sh alone into a bin directory also copy the library to bin/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh beside it: tests/lib/project-storage.sh:10-11, tests/lib/herdr.py:598 and :616, tests/session-startup.test.sh:123, tests/lib/autopilot_entrypoints.py:29-34 (its fixed bin/lib list) and tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts:99-104 (its fixed bin/lib list); tests/e2e/board-crew.spec.ts:51, which pins the exact bin/lib listing of that fixture, adds fm-task-grammar.sh to its sorted list, and its comment at :40-46 gains one line saying the board fixture holds the task grammar library because fm-emit.sh sources it, and that the library only defines shell functions and reaches no model. Every other fixture that copies fm-emit.sh already copies all of bin/lib or calls project_storage_fixture. A branch may carry one leading path segment before the task id: the JavaScript copy becomes /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\/)?([tT]|[sS][kK])-?([0-9]{3,})(-.*)?$/ (capture indices unchanged); the bash copy, which is POSIX ERE with no `(?:` group and spells every bracket set out (fm-emit.sh:33), becomes re="^([${FM_TASK_UP}${FM_TASK_LOW}${FM_TASK_DIG}._-]+/)?([tT]|[sS][kK])-?([${FM_TASK_DIG}]{3,})(-.*)?$" with the prefix and digits read from BASH_REMATCH[2] and BASH_REMATCH[3] (FM_TASK_UP/FM_TASK_LOW sit above fm_task_of_branch in the library so they are defined before it); both copies read so `feature/t-001-x` is T-001, `feature/sk-002-y` is SK-002, `feature/t-1170-z` is T-1170, while `a/b/t-001` (two segments), `/t-001` and `hotfix/x` name no task. This is generic, not per-project configuration, so every reader stays one call: bin/fm-merge.sh:102-104, bin/fm-decide.sh:320, bin/lib/fm_adopt.py:116, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:86 and fm-emit's own merged-event check at :175 all go through `fm_task_of_branch`/`fm_task_of_pr` and need no edit. `fm_task_of_title` is unchanged.

Change 5, the remaining copies of the branch reading. bin/fm-reconcile.sh:350-351 `task_of` sources bin/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh (never bin/fm-emit.sh, which tests/reconcile.test.sh:369, :767-811 and :918-923 replace with a stub writer) and returns `fm_task_of_branch` instead of its own sed. This closes the `task_of` half of the open item in design/design.md §5.2 :342-345 (reconcile reading `t-1170-…` as T-117 and missing `sk-…`). Its `is_task_id` at :136 (pid-file names, only `T-<3 digits>`) is unchanged, and the design keeps that half of the open item open. bin/lib/fm_stack.py has four branch readers and each accepts the same one optional leading `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/` segment: `select_base` (:61) strips it from the lowercased headRefName before its `^<dep>(-|$)` match; `release_parent` (:71) and `restack` (:94) allow it in their `^(?:t|sk)-\d+(?:-|$)` task-branch checks (protected names main, master, HEAD and the base stay refused); the restack command (:239) reads the task from the part after the optional segment. So a stacked child on `feature/t-…` restacks and a merged parent on `feature/t-…` is deletable under the existing delete_branch rule; these paths are reached from bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:369 and :570.

Change 6, onboarding (bin/lib/fm_onboard.py). `inspect_remote` (:59-99) also reads, through the same `observed` contents calls: `.drone.yml`, `.drone.jsonnet`, every local jsonnet file that `.drone.jsonnet` imports by a plain relative name (import 'x.jsonnet', one level, at most 5 files), and the `.github/workflows` directory listing plus each `*.yml`/`*.yaml` file in it (at most 20). It records them under evidence `ci_files`. `infer` (:121) proposes `ci_branch_patterns` (every `refs/heads/...` string and every `branch:`/`branches:` list item found in those files, deduplicated, `refs/tags/*` and tag-only entries dropped), `ci_pull_request` (true when a drone trigger lists event pull_request or a workflow has an `on.pull_request` or `on: [pull_request]` trigger), and `branch_prefix` (the most common first path segment plus `/` among the last 30 pull request head branches; when patterns were found, only heads that match a pattern count; when no patterns were found, every head with a segment counts; none when no head has a segment), each with its cited evidence (file paths and pull request numbers). `questions` (:181-192) adds them to the policy question's evidence. `approve` (:270-300) accepts the three fields only from the captain's answers, exactly like pr_title (:278-286): inspected or proposed values are dropped first. `edit` (:316-322) accepts the three fields. Parsing is plain text and regex: no YAML or jsonnet evaluation. A `.github/workflows` answer that is not a list (a file answer, an error, unknown) is recorded as unknown and adds no workflow files. Migration: `infer` treats evidence without `ci_files` (records written before this task, read by `drift` at :337 through the timed watcher bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:88, and by bin/fm-canary.sh:670-673) as no CI evidence: it proposes no ci_branch_patterns and no ci_pull_request, proposes branch_prefix from the pull request heads by the no-patterns rule above, and never raises; `drift` does not compare the three new proposals (they are captain-confirmed fields, not drift keys).

Changed attribution, stated. A branch a person names `<segment>/t-NNN-…` or `<segment>/sk-NNN-…` now names that task wherever the grammar is read: bin/lib/fm_adopt.py:114-121 refuses adopting such a pull request for a different task (it accepted it before), and the autopilot (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:86), fm-decide, fm-merge and reconcile attribute it to that task. No adoption is in flight on any managed project today; an in-flight adoption whose branch now names another task is refused at its next round by the existing check, which is the intended rule. For an external project, a malformed owner default file now stops the worker with exit 65 and the Change 2 refusal before any worktree, push or pull request; before this task the worker warned and used the generic fallback. Not changed, stated. The self project branch names, PR titles and grammar results for every existing unprefixed branch; gate 1 and every gate (they take the branch from the PR); the T-119 merged-event refusal semantics; existing external pull requests on `t-NNN-work` (nothing renames them, and they keep resolving to their task); post modes and PR text (T-247).

Tests, new behaviour (each fails on the base commit and passes after). New tests/external-branch-prefix.test.sh running tests/lib/external_branch_prefix.py against bin/fm-worker.sh with the existing external fixture style (git remotes on disk, a gh stub that answers `pr view --json headRefName` and `pr create` exactly as gh prints them): (1) branch_prefix "feature/" and a public_title give `feature/t-051-<slug of the title>` and the pull request is opened from it; (2) the owner default file supplies the prefix when CONVENTIONS lacks it, and a CONVENTIONS value beats it; (3) an existing remote `feature/t-051-x` branch is found by the guess and reused; (4) patterns ["refs/heads/feature/*"] with a `feature/` prefix pass; (5) patterns ["release/*"], ci_pull_request false and a `feature/` prefix: exit 65, the refusal text, a worker_crashed event, no push and no pull request; (6) the same with ci_pull_request true passes; (7) patterns absent: the warning line and the round continues; (8) fm_conventions.py validate refuses bad branch_prefix values ("feature", "../", "a/b/", "-x/") and a non-list ci_branch_patterns, and refuses ci_branch_patterns in an owner file; `--field branch_format` prints the documented JSON. tests/board-task-grammar.test.sh table rows (shell and TypeScript must agree): feature/t-001-x→T-001, FEATURE/T-001→T-001, feature/sk-002-y→SK-002, feature/t-1170-z→T-1170; and a pair row feature/t-005-x with title "T-009: …"→T-005. tests/reconcile.test.sh: a merged PR on `feature/t-021-x` reconciles to T-021 and one on `sk-002-y` to SK-002. tests/stacking_cases.py: select_base finds a parent PR on `feature/t-1-parent`; restack accepts a child on `feature/t-2-child`; release_parent deletes a merged parent on `feature/t-1-parent` under delete_branch. tests/lib/external_adopt.py (run by tests/external-adopt.test.sh): adopting a PR on `feature/t-001-x` for T-001 is accepted, and for T-002 is refused with "names another task". Worker case (9): a public_title that fails fm_public_text.validate gives `<prefix>t-051-work`. Worker case (10), also in tests/lib/external_branch_prefix.py: a malformed owner file makes the worker exit 65 with the Change 2 refusal (both languages), a worker_crashed event and no push. tests/onboarding.test.sh also: a workflows directory answer that is not a list is recorded as unknown; infer on evidence without ci_files proposes no patterns, proposes `feature/` from heads [feature/a, feature/b, fix/c], and does not raise; with patterns ["release/*"] and the same heads it proposes no branch_prefix. tests/onboarding.test.sh: with a gh stub that answers the contents API like GitHub (a file as {encoding:'base64', content}, a directory as a list of {name, path, type}), inspection records ci_files from .drone.yml, an imported jsonnet file and a workflow; infer proposes the three fields with evidence; approve drops proposed values unless answered and keeps answered ones; edit accepts them.

Tests, regression (pass on base and after). tests/external-execution.test.sh:262-272 still sees `t-051-work` (no prefix configured); tests/board-task-grammar.test.sh existing rows and the rows a/b/t-001→none, /t-001→none and hotfix/x→none (shell and TypeScript agree; these already hold on base); tests/stacking_cases.py: release_parent still refuses `feature` alone, main, master and the base; tests/reconcile.test.sh cases that replace fm-emit.sh with a stub (:369, :767-811, :918-923); tests/herdr-emitstatus.test.sh, tests/session-startup.test.sh, tests/autopilot-entrypoints.test.sh (tests/lib/autopilot_entrypoints.py) and the e2e suites that use tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts; tests/diagram.test.sh grammar lift (:788-1013); tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py (`t-001-work` and `human-work` heads); tests/external-pr-format.test.sh; tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh; tests/reconcile.test.sh existing cases; tests/stacking_cases.py existing cases; tests/stacking.test.sh; tests/stacking-restack.test.sh; tests/external-adopt.test.sh existing cases; tests/conventions-watch.test.sh (drift on old inspection records).

Callers, all listed. Branch grammar: bin/fm-emit.sh:41-59 and :175; board/server.ts:617-662 (taskOfBranch, taskOfPr) and the grammar text served in front of board/public/diagram.js (owned ids only, unaffected); bin/fm-merge.sh:102-104; bin/fm-decide.sh:320; bin/lib/fm_adopt.py:116; bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:86; bin/fm-reconcile.sh:350-351 (changed) and :422; bin/lib/fm_stack.py:61, :71, :94 and :239 (all changed), reached from bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:369 and :570; bin/lib/fm_onboard.py drift (:332-340) via bin/lib/fm_conventions_watch.py:88. Worker branch: bin/fm-worker.sh:417-461 (guess, adopt, --pr headRefName, new name), :506 (round_two from branch_guess). Conventions: bin/lib/fm_conventions.py:13-147 and its wrapper bin/fm-config.sh:1140-1146; bin/lib/fm_onboard.py approve/edit/inspect/infer/questions and bin/fm-canary.sh:673 (calls approve with answers lacking the new keys; unchanged behaviour).

Migration. CONVENTIONS without the new fields: no prefix (branch stays `$slug-work`), and Change 3 prints the warning and continues. firstmate adds the fields to each managed project through `fm_onboard.py edit` after this merges, with the captain-confirmed values; that edit is not part of this task. Existing pull requests and branches are never renamed. Pins: CONVENTIONS is snapshotted but not compared (bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py), so no repin is needed.

Docs. design/design.md: in §5.2 (heading at :249), the task-grammar paragraph "One task-id grammar (T-119)" at about :320-346 names bin/lib/fm-task-grammar.sh as the home of the shell grammar, states the optional leading segment, and rewrites the open item at :342-345 so only its `is_task_id` half stays open; §15.2 (heading at about :5119) lists the three fields and the owner default for branch_prefix; §15.7 (heading at about :5490) states the branch name rule and the CI trigger check, and its owner-file paragraph at about :5519-5533 changes "only these three keys" to the three pr_* keys and branch_prefix, and replaces "the worker warn and use the generic fallback" with the exit-65 refusal for a malformed owner file. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md (the external spec paragraph at about :982-999): change the sentence at :997-999 that says owner files "allow only those three keys" to say they allow the three pr_* keys and branch_prefix; onboarding confirms branch_prefix and the CI patterns; a round refuses a branch that no CI pattern matches.

intent.text: A new external branch uses the confirmed prefix of its repository, so the repository CI runs on it.
A round refuses a new branch that no recorded CI trigger pattern matches.
Firstmate still finds the task of a prefixed branch everywhere.
Onboarding reads the CI trigger files and recent branches, and proposes the prefix with evidence.

why.text: The captain said on 2026-10-07 that the branch t-001-work did not trigger CI.
Today a new external branch is always named t-NNN-work.
Today the task grammar reads a task id only at the start of a branch name.

scope_in: bin/fm-worker.sh: the branch name and the CI check
bin/fm-emit.sh and board/server.ts: the task grammar

done.text: Intent 1: the worker builds the prefixed branch name. Test cases 1, 2 and 3 prove it.
Intent 2: the worker matches the branch against the patterns before any push. Test cases 4 to 7 prove it.
Intent 3: the grammar accepts one leading segment. The grammar, reconcile and stacking cases prove it.
Intent 4: onboarding records the CI files and proposes the three fields. The onboarding cases prove it.

notes.text: A push to a matching branch can also start a deploy step in that CI.
Firstmate never renames a branch that already has a pull request.

intent.text: 新的外部分支使用 repo 確認過的前綴，CI 會執行。
新分支不符合任何 CI 觸發規則時，回合會拒絕。
firstmate 在各處都能讀出帶前綴分支的任務。
onboarding 讀 CI 觸發檔和近期分支，附證據提出前綴。

why.text: 船長在 2026-10-07 指出 t-001-work 分支沒有觸發 CI。
現在新的外部分支一律叫 t-NNN-work。
現在任務文法只從分支名稱開頭讀任務編號。

scope_in: bin/fm-worker.sh：分支名稱和 CI 檢查
bin/fm-reconcile.sh 和 bin/lib/fm_stack.py：讀分支的程式

done.text: 意圖 1：worker 組出帶前綴的分支名稱。案例 1、2、3 證明。
意圖 2：worker 在推送前比對分支和規則。案例 4 到 7 證明。
意圖 3：文法接受一段前綴。文法、reconcile 和 stacking 案例證明。
意圖 4：onboarding 記錄 CI 檔並提出三個欄位。onboarding 案例證明。

notes.text: 推到符合的分支也會啟動該 CI 的部署步驟。
firstmate 不會重新命名已有 PR 的分支。
